subject: Post-call: SLO & context capacity for Kairos streaming use case
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ross <sam.ross@kairoshealth.com>, Alicia Trent <alicia.trent@kairoshealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: SLO targets, context sizes, next steps

Hi Sam / Alicia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track decisions and open items. Appreciate you confirming priorities on the call.

Key notes from today
- Primary user flow: real-time summary + context-aware suggestions inside clinician UI. Client will stream patient notes incrementally and expect token-level partial outputs (streaming generation).
- Expected per-request token mix: ~6,000 tokens input (historical context + recent notes) and up to ~1,000 tokens output for generated summary / suggestions in the worst case. Typical median will be smaller (~2k input, 200 output).
- Concurrency target: initial pilot aims for 25 concurrent active sessions, growth target 50. Peak bursts up to ~120 concurrent requests for short windows (90s).
- Latency SLOs: goal is p95 end-to-end generation <= 300ms for the 2k/200 median case; for the 6k/1k case we understand higher tail latency is acceptable, but need guidance on expected degradation and fallback behavior.

Questions / asks for Kairos (please confirm):
1) Are the sample traffic percentages in the attached CSV representative of 95%/median/peak?
2) Can you share whether client-side streaming expects first-token delivery within X ms (we recommend <150–200ms for a good UX)?
3) Any regulatory constraints on model variants or quantization (e.g., must avoid 4-bit quantization due to internal review)?

Proposed Redwood plan
- Short term: run two replication load tests against hosted Dedicated-like config: (A) baseline model (fp16, native kernels) and (B) quantized variant (8-bit/4-bit depending on constraints). We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and first-byte time.
- Implement prefix caching for stable patient history chunks to reduce repeated compute for large contexts.
- Canary rollout: start pilot with 25 concurrency and traffic shaping to simulate spikes. Provide a runbook for graceful fallback to a lower-context variant that trims older context if p95 > target.

Next steps / owners
- Sam / Alicia: confirm CSV is representative and share any additional traffic patterns by EOD Thur 9/16. (attachment: sample-traffic-agg.csv)
- Redwood (Connor): propose load test config and runbook by 9/16.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare quantization/variant performance notes and a short risk table by 9/17.

Attachments: kairos-slo-questionnaire.pdf (we filled fields we discussed), sample-traffic-agg.csv

Thanks — I'll consolidate the answers and schedule the load test.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
https://redwood.com
From: Sam Ross <sam.ross@kairoshealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Trent <alicia.trent@kairoshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO targets, context sizes, next steps

Thanks Marissa — that summary looks great and matches our internal notes. Quick clarifications:

- The CSV is representative of production-ish batch logs (we over-sampled peak traffic for safety). Median case is indeed ~2k input / 150–250 output tokens. The 6k input / 1k output is our upper bound for long patient histories.
- Streaming expectations: clinicians want first partial token within ~150ms of request start to keep the UI responsive (we can tolerate longer tail for long-context generations).
- Compliance: we can't use 4-bit quantization for PHI-heavy content without internal reviewer sign-off; 8-bit is usually okay but we need to see tradeoffs.

We attached an example transcript (on the drive link in the thread) that shows the chunking behavior of the client — the client sends incremental blocks of the current note and expects partial streaming as soon as model returns tokens.

I'll aim to return a short traffic heatmap and a user session slice by 9/16 EOD. If you can propose the load test config, we can align on a test window next week.

Sam
Sam Ross
Product Lead, Integrations | Kairos Health
sam.ross@kairoshealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ross <sam.ross@kairoshealth.com>, Alicia Trent <alicia.trent@kairoshealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO targets, context sizes, next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Sam. Connor / Ben — looping you both in with the confirmed expectations. High-level technical takeaways for the internal plan:

- Streaming first-byte target: we will optimize for <150ms first-byte for median flows by prioritizing request routing to low-latency pool and enabling incremental KV cache hits for recent context chunks.
- Large-context handling: for the 6k input cases we propose two hedges: (1) progressive truncation strategy that preserves the most recent N tokens (configurable, default preserve last 2,000 tokens) and (2) a quantized fallback endpoint (8-bit) that keeps correctness but reduces compute time — only enabled after load test validation and Kairos sign-off on compliance.
- Concurrency shaping: we recommend connection-level queueing and a soft concurrency cap per-user to keep p95 stable. We'll simulate bursts up to 120 qps but recommend a throttling policy at 80 qps for initial rollout.

Load test plan (Connor lead):
- Two baseline model shapes: fp16 (gold) and 8-bit quantized (candidate).
- Traffic profile: use attached CSV to parameterize 3 mixes: median (70%), heavy (25%), and extreme burst (5%). Ramp to target concurrency over 5m windows. Capture first-byte times, p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, and per-token CPU/GPU utilization.
- Success criteria: median p95 <=300ms for median mix; degradation slope for long-context should be documented with suggested trimming thresholds.

Ben: can you prepare a short doc on expected latency delta vs context size (empirical numbers for our current models) and list any model variants we should avoid for PHI? That will help compliance decisioning.

Sam / Alicia: once we have the load test results we'll propose a canary traffic window and rollback thresholds. Planning note: we'd like permission to run an initial smoke test in your staging environment to validate end-to-end streaming hooks — is that OK?

I'll set up a Calendly slot for the load test coordination.

Cheers,
Marissa
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Ross <sam.ross@kairoshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO targets, context sizes, next steps

Thanks — I have a draft runbook and load-test config ready. Short notes and actions:

- Runbook highlights: test buckets (median/heavy/extreme), measurement hooks (first-byte, p50/p95/p99, kv-cache-hit-rate), fallback triggers (p95 delta > 2x baseline or GPU util > 85% for 3 consecutive minutes).
- Preliminary numbers to expect (ballpark): for a 2k input / 200 output request on our fp16 baseline we typically see p95 ~180–230ms on an A100-style node; for 6k/1k it climbs to ~550–900ms depending on kernel selection and batching. 8-bit quant often reduces p95 by ~20–35% on larger contexts but needs validation on PHI datasets.
- Action items:
  * Connor: schedule a 60m load-test window and share test harness (link in related_links). Target Wed 9/22 08:00–09:00 PT for initial run if that works for Kairos.
  * Ben: drop the quantization risk table in the shared drive by 9/17.
  * Sam: confirm staging access and a sample user session by 9/16 EOD.

Sam — can you confirm the proposed test slot? If not, propose 2 alternatives and we'll adapt.

Thanks
Connor O'Brien
